ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening before incorporation and on a continuous risk-based basis against the European Union consolidated asset-freezing and financial sanctions list, United Nations Security Council sanctions, OFAC SDN list for USD transactions and US-connected activity, and the Spanish domestic terrorist-financing and sanctions lists. Politically Exposed Persons are screened in accordance with Article 14 of Ley 10/2010 and AMLD/5AMLD definitions, including senior officials of Spanish, EU and international public institutions, family members and known close associates. Enhanced customer due diligence is mandatory for PEPs, high-risk third countries, and any unusual ownership structure.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) - official name clearance service for Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social at www.rmc.es
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed in Spanish or in a co-official Spanish language (Catalan, Galician, Basque, Valencian). If a foreign name is used, it must be transliterated or adapted to the Spanish alphabet and must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company. The name must be lawful, truthful, not contrary to public order, and must not mislead as to the company's activity or legal form.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: ESPAÑA or denominations of the State, autonomous communities, provinces and municipalities without specific administrative authorization
GOBIERNO, ADMINISTRACIÓN, MINISTERIO, SECRETARÍA DE ESTADO, DIRECCIÓN GENERAL, AYUNTAMIENTO, DIPUTACIÓN
INSTITUTO, UNIVERSIDAD, COLEGIO PROFESIONAL, CÁMARA OFICIAL, FUNDACIÓN or any expression suggesting official or public character

BANCO, CAJA, CRÉDITO, FINANCIAMIENTO, INVERSIÓN, FONDO, GARANTÍA, SEGURO, REASEGURO and similar regulated financial-sector tokens requiring prior authorization from the Bank of Spain, the Directorate General of Insurance and Pension Funds, or the CNMV
SA, SL, SLL, SLU, S.A., S.L., S.L.L. or abbreviations capable of misrepresenting the actual legal form of the company
Words contrary to law, morality, or public order, or that are identical or confusingly similar to an existing trademark or registered company name
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection by the Registro Mercantil Central, the applicant may file an optional reconsideration request (recurso de reposición) with the RMC within 15 business days of notification. Alternatively, or after reconsideration is dismissed, the applicant may file an administrative appeal (recurso de alzada) before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (DGSJFP) within one month of the rejection. The appeal must state the grounds of unlawfulness, attach the negative certificate and supporting evidence, and may suggest alternative candidate names. It is prudent to apply for at least three ranked name alternatives to avoid delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office address is permissible for an SL engaged in remote screen-sharing and IoT telemetry software if the address corresponds to a physically existing location in Spain and is capable of receiving legal notifications and administrative service. A PO Box is not sufficient. For a low-risk software business, no special license is required for the virtual office, but the company should maintain substantive local activity such as board resolutions, accounting records, commercial contracts, technical development or support staff, and a real domicile for legal notices in order to avoid a challenge as a letterbox company under Spanish CFC and economic-substance rules.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for a remote software/IoT company, with estimated annual probability of unannounced physical inspection at 5% to 10%. Probability increases materially to 25% to 40% if the company claims recurrent VAT refunds, invoices related-party foreign transactions, has no local employees or directors, or uses a non-compliant mail-forwarding address. Inspections may be carried out by the Spanish Tax Agency (AEAT), SEPBLAC, or the labor inspectorate.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Spanish Capital Companies Act (Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio – Ley de Sociedades de Capital), arts. 20-33 (formation), art. 4 (minimum capital), art. 22 (public deed and registration), arts. 62-82 (limited liability company rules).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (name certification) and Registro Mercantil Provincial of the company's registered office (definitive registration).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura de Constitución (notarized public deed of incorporation) inscribed in the Registro Mercantil.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital of EUR 3,000 (approx. USD 3,250), fully subscribed and paid in cash in a Spanish bank account or through an expert-valuated non-cash contribution. A bank certificate (certificado de desembolso) must be delivered to the notary prior to the deed being granted.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: The founding partners approve the deed of incorporation and the articles of association, irrevocably subscribing and paying in the share capital as set out in the capital schedule. The registered office is fixed at [street, postal code, city, Spain], recorded with the Mercantile Registry and tax authorities. Appointed officers: [Name, DNI] as sole administrator and [Name] as secretary, if applicable. The officers are expressly authorized to obtain the provisional NIF, open corporate bank accounts, and execute all statutory filings. Adopted unanimously on [date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Certification at the Central Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (online portal / provincial registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit form VN-1 to the Central Mercantile Registry, either online or at any provincial registry, to obtain a negative name certificate (certificación negativa de denominación) confirming that the proposed corporate name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered entity. Provide up to five alternative names in order of preference.
required_dossiers: NIF/DNI or passport copy of each founding partner
Power of attorney, if filing through a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected because the name conflicts with an existing registration, the next preferred alternative from the submitted list shall be used, or a fresh name certificate application shall be filed. An administrative appeal may be lodged within one month if the rejection is erroneous.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of Share Capital in a Spanish Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish credit institution (authorized bank / escrow provider)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary account in the name of the future company ('[Company Name], S.L. en constitución') at a Spanish bank, deposit the minimum paid-up capital of EUR 3,000, and obtain a certificate of deposit (certificado de desembolso). In the event of non-cash contributions, an external expert valuation report must be prepared and annexed to the deed.
required_dossiers: Negative name certificate (certificación negativa de denominación)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to open the temporary account due to naming issues, rectify the name certificate and re-apply. Alternatively, the capital may be deposited with the notary acting as escrow agent (depósito notarial) subject to notary acceptance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Granting of the Public Deed before a Spanish Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founding partners (or their legal representatives) must appear before the chosen notary, provide the bank capital certificate and identification documents, and sign the public deed of incorporation (escritura de constitución). The notary verifies legal capacity, statutory requirements, and gives an authenticated first copy (copia autorizada) for filing with the Mercantile Registry.
required_dossiers: Bank certificate of capital deposit (certificado de desembolso)
Statement of proposed registered address, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies deficiencies in the draft deed, a supplementary notarial act (acta complementaria) must be executed to correct the wording. Missing documents, such as the bank certificate, must be supplied before signing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) – local tax office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the deed is granted, file form 036/037 with the AEAT to obtain the provisional NIF (NIF provisional). This tax identification number is required to transact with public authorities and to complete the final registry step. The provisional NIF remains valid until the definitive NIF is issued after Mercantile Registry registration.
required_dossiers: First copy (copia autorizada) of the public deed of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEAT issues a request for amendment or additional documentation, resubmit the corrected form and provide standardized statutory information. In urgent cases, a tax representative can process the NIF through the AEAT electronic registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration in the Provincial Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial corresponding to the company's registered office (e.g., Registro Mercantil de Madrid)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized first copy of the incorporation deed (copia autorizada) with the competent Provincial Mercantile Registry within two months of grant. The registrar examines the deed and articles for legal conformity. Once the registration is effected, the company acquires full legal personality. After registration, obtain a certified registry extract (certificación registral) and present it to the AEAT to finalize the definitive NIF.
required_dossiers: First copy of the notarized public deed
Proof of payment of registry fees (aranceles)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a negative qualification (calificación negativa), submit a correction brief (instancia de subsanación) to the registry addressing each defect. If the defect is substantive, execute a supplementary notarial act and re-file. If the registrar's decision is contested unsuccessfully, file an appeal to the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública within two months.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial licensing board applies to ISIC 6201 (remote desktop access software and IoT telemetry). Relevant oversight may include the Spanish Data Protection Agency (AEPD) for privacy compliance and the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Digital Transformation for telecommunications aspects.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No mandatory operating or manufacturing license is required for software development, remote support, or cloud-based telemetry services. Industries may seek voluntary certifications such as ISO/IEC 27001 or ENS (Esquema Nacional de Seguridad) for public-sector contracts.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not applicable for purely software activities. If future hardware/datacenter operations begin, the competent agency is the Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (MITERD) and the regional autonomous community environmental authority.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — software development and remote digital services fall outside the mandatory EIA categories under Law 21/2013 (Ley de Evaluación Ambiental). No EIA is required at incorporation stage.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable. For future physical premises, compliance with municipal wastewater discharge limits, VOC controls under Royal Decree 117/2003, and electronic waste segregation under Law 22/2011 (RAEE) would be required.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For any commercial or industrial premises, a municipal activity license (licencia de actividad) or prior communication (comunicación previa) is required. Fire prevention certification (boletín de prevención y extinción de incendios) is required for premises over 200 m2 or specific hazard classes. Workplace risk prevention assessment (Ley 31/1995 de Prevención de Riesgos Laborales) and occupational medical clearance are mandatory for all employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) – Sede Electrónica: sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada obtains a definitive NIF/CIF upon incorporation before the Commercial Registry and AEAT. Foreign entities without a permanent establishment must apply for a non-resident NIF using Form 030 and, if required, register for Spanish VAT using Form 036/037. VAT identification for cross-border transactions is obtained via the VIES registration process after completing the applicable AEAT census filing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Not applicable: an SL is mandatorily subject to Spanish Corporate Income Tax with no check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections. Optional group taxation regime (régimen de consolidación fiscal) is available to Spanish-resident corporate groups where the parent holds at least 75% of the capital of qualifying subsidiaries.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido) – Spanish Value Added Tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No minimum turnover threshold: any taxable person carrying out economic activities in Spain must register for VAT before making their first taxable supply. Optional simplified and small-business regimes are limited to certain individual entrepreneurs and do not apply to a standard limited-liability entity.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Business-to-business electronic invoicing is mandatory under Law 18/2022 and Royal Decree 1007/2023. Large taxpayers with turnover exceeding EUR 8,000,000 must submit immediate VAT information through AEAT's SII platform using XML/API within 4 calendar days of invoice issuance. VERI*FACTU digital stamping and QR-code verification for consumer-facing invoices is required once the technical implementing order is fully in force.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods to destinations outside the EU qualify for a 0% VAT exemption with credit (Art. 21 of the Spanish VAT Law). For remote-support software and IoT telemetry services, B2B supplies to non-EU customers are outside the scope of Spanish VAT under the place-of-supply rule for intangible services; B2C digital services supplied to customers established outside the EU are also outside Spanish VAT. Input VAT attributable to such export or non-EU service activity is deductible, provided the taxpayer retains evidence of the customer's identity, business status, country of residence, and payment flow.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DEX) for physical goods – not applicable to pure remote software/IoT services unless tangible media or hardware is supplied
Bill of Lading / CMR / Airwaybill for physical export shipments – not applicable to digital-only services
Commercial contract and itemised invoices identifying the non-EU customer and the software/IoT service
Evidence of the customer's establishment and business status (e.g., foreign VAT registration number, tax ID, or equivalent legal certificate)
Bank payment and foreign-exchange remittance confirmation (Inward Remittance Certificate) evidencing actual receipt of remuneration
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT may conduct targeted inspections of export zero-rating and place-of-supply claims. Fraudulent claims lead to retrospective assessment of unreported VAT plus late-payment interest and an economic penalty of 50% to 150% of the tax amount; where deliberate bad faith is proven, the penalty surcharge can reach 120% on the net tax. Criminal prosecution under Article 305 of the Criminal Code applies for tax evasion exceeding EUR 120,000, with potential prison sentences and additional fines.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España, within the Eurosystem; foreign-exchange and international-investment reporting is also administered under the authority of the Spanish Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business. The European Central Bank is the monetary authority for the euro area.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain uses the euro and has no general capital-account or current-account exchange controls. Residents and non-residents may generally hold euro and foreign-currency accounts, make cross-border payments, receive foreign investment, distribute dividends, repay shareholder loans, and repatriate capital without prior foreign-exchange approval. Restrictions may nevertheless arise from EU sanctions, anti-money-laundering controls, beneficial-ownership verification, tax-clearance requirements, withholding-tax rules, transfer-pricing rules, corporate-law distribution tests, and bank-specific source-of-funds procedures. Dividends and other profit distributions require distributable accounting profits, compliance with Spanish Companies Act reserve and net-equity requirements, and appropriate withholding-tax analysis. EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief, treaty relief, or domestic exemptions may be available but normally require beneficial-owner, holding-period, participation, tax-residence, and anti-abuse evidence. Cross-border payments and investments may be reportable for statistical or foreign-investment purposes even where no authorization is required.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain has no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion ratio. Export receipts may remain in foreign currency or be converted into euros at the holder's discretion, subject to contractual, accounting, tax, sanctions, and AML requirements. Goods and services exporters should retain invoices, contracts, shipping or service-delivery evidence, customer identification, payment records, and reconciliation files. Cross-border payment and international-investment information may be required for Banco de España statistical reporting or Ministry of Economy foreign-investment declarations, depending on transaction type, thresholds, counterparty location, and applicable reporting rules. Export VAT and customs records must be reconciled independently from treasury records.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Deposit Account for incorporation or capital increase, followed by an Operational Current Account
Capital Deposit Account for incorporation or capital increase, followed by an Operational Current Account
Capital Deposit Account for incorporation or capital increase, followed by an Operational Current Account
Capital Deposit Account for incorporation or capital increase, followed by an Operational Current Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for payment collection, SEPA transfers, card acquiring, and multi-currency treasury; Low as the sole operating bank for an early-stage Spanish SL. An EU-licensed electronic money institution or payment institution may passport services into Spain under PSD2, but must verify licensing, passporting or Spanish establishment status, safeguarding arrangements, operational resilience, limits, local IBAN availability, chargeback controls, and support for tax, payroll, supplier, and capital transactions. An offshore non-EEA digital EMI generally cannot provide regulated payment services in Spain without an EU authorization, licensed EU agent, or appropriate Spanish establishment. Fintech accounts may not support Spanish incorporation capital certificates, notarized capital evidence, cash-intensive activity, complex shareholder loans, or high-value SWIFT transactions. Maintain a Tier 1 Spanish bank as the primary account and use the EMI as a controlled collection or payment sub-rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Spanish banks may permit remote onboarding for eligible companies and authorized representatives using qualified electronic identification, video identification, digital certificates, or branch-supported processes. Physical attendance is not universally mandated by statute, but a bank may require an in-person meeting or original-document review for non-resident directors, complex ownership, high-risk jurisdictions, unusual business models, foreign-source capital, or failed remote verification. The bank must identify the SL, directors, authorized signatories, ultimate beneficial owners, controllers, business purpose, expected activity, source of funds, and tax-residence information. Obtain a Spanish NIF, deed of incorporation, Commercial Registry evidence, beneficial-owner declaration, powers of attorney, and tax forms before requesting full transactional capability.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident or layered ownership that prevents clear identification of the ultimate beneficial owner or controller.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current organizational chart to natural-person ownership; certified passports and address evidence for each relevant owner and director; shareholder-register extracts; incorporation documents for intermediate entities; UBO declaration; control-rights analysis; board resolutions; and, where applicable, apostilled or legalized corporate documents with Spanish translations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business description is inconsistent with the stated activity, transaction profile, or remote-support software model.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Concise business plan; product and technical description; website and customer terms; software licensing and subscription agreements; sample invoices; customer and supplier geographies; expected monthly volumes; payment-rail map; data-protection and information-security policies; and written confirmation that the company does not provide regulated financial, gambling, telecom, or cybersecurity services unless separately authorized.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained foreign capital injection, shareholder loan, or transfer from an unrelated third party.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed capital subscription or shareholder-loan agreement; shareholder or board resolution; sending-bank evidence; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statement; audited or filed financial statements of the funder where relevant; tax-residence certificates; beneficial-owner evidence; payment purpose; and reconciliation to the Spanish accounting ledger and, where applicable, foreign-investment reporting.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected cross-border volumes, Latin American counterparties, or payment flows inconsistent with a low-risk software profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Country and counterparty matrix; sanctions-screening procedure; customer onboarding policy; transaction-monitoring rules; contracts and invoices; service-delivery evidence; transfer-pricing policy; expected FX exposures; and management certification that funds are not collected or transmitted for third parties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of personal accounts, virtual IBANs, payment aggregators, or multiple fintech providers without transparent reconciliation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Treasury policy prohibiting personal accounts; approved-bank register; account ownership evidence; provider licenses; safeguarding and settlement descriptions; daily reconciliation procedures; payment-flow diagrams; segregation-of-funds controls; and documented rationale for every fintech account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete tax-residence, FATCA, CRS, or beneficial-ownership information.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Spanish NIF and tax registration evidence; CRS self-certification; FATCA classification; director and UBO tax-residence certificates; foreign TINs; corporate tax classification; and confirmation of registered office, operating address, and management location.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdictions, sanctioned parties, politically exposed persons, adverse media, or unusual IP and cybersecurity concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent sanctions and PEP screening; enhanced due-diligence report; beneficial-owner verification; source-of-wealth evidence; adverse-media resolution; customer-risk approval; contractual termination rights; access-control and logging policy; incident-response policy; and legal confirmation that the product is not used to facilitate prohibited remote access.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route paid-in capital through a Spanish Tier 1 bank account opened in the name of the SL, using the bank's stated capital-contribution purpose and the exact legal name and NIF of the company. The remitter should be the subscriber or documented shareholder, not an unexplained third party. Use SEPA Credit Transfer for euro funding from the EEA and SWIFT MT103 or ISO 20022 equivalent for non-SEPA currencies. Include shareholder name, subscription or loan reference, company NIF, and purpose narrative. Obtain the bank's capital-deposit certificate where required for incorporation or capital increase; retain the notarial deed, shareholder resolution, subscription schedule, sending-bank confirmation, and ledger reconciliation. Distinguish equity, shareholder loans, management fees, and ordinary revenue. Review whether the transaction triggers Spanish foreign-investment reporting, Banco de España statistical reporting, CRS/FATCA classification, withholding, or transfer-pricing documentation. Do not split transfers to avoid bank controls.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible euro suppliers and payroll; use SWIFT MT103 or ISO 20022 cross-border payment instructions for non-SEPA currencies. For recurring software, cloud, hosting, and professional-service suppliers, maintain approved-vendor records, contracts, purchase orders, invoices, tax status, sanctions screening, and three-way reconciliation. For goods imports, retain commercial invoice, customs declaration, transport evidence, Incoterms, and import VAT or duty records. Commercial letters of credit may be issued through a Spanish bank under UCP 600, with documentary collections under URC 522 where suitable. Banks may request purpose, beneficiary ownership, invoice, contract, shipping evidence, and sanctions information before release. Reconcile payment execution, bank fees, FX rate, VAT treatment, and accounting entries. Apply withholding-tax analysis to non-resident service, royalty, interest, and other payments before remittance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward exchange contracts with an authorized bank for documented forecast or committed receivables and payables, subject to suitability, ISDA or bank terms, collateral, valuation, and accounting controls.

Non-deliverable forwards for currencies or corridors where physical delivery is restricted or impractical, subject to bank eligibility, applicable local-market rules, sanctions screening, and documented underlying exposure.

Currency swaps and cross-currency interest-rate swaps for documented funding or balance-sheet exposures, subject to MiFID-related conduct requirements, appropriateness or suitability processes, master documentation, collateral, valuation, and counterparty limits.

FX options, collars, and participating forwards may be used only under a board-approved hedging policy with documented exposure, maximum premium and downside parameters, accounting treatment, and senior-approval thresholds.

Permissible instruments must be entered into with regulated banks or authorized investment firms, not unlicensed offshore counterparties. The SL should prohibit speculative trading, maintain hedge-designation records where hedge accounting is used, monitor EMIR reporting or clearing obligations where applicable, and document mark-to-market, collateral, counterparty, and liquidity risks.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary General Meeting (Junta General Ordinaria) — approval of annual accounts for the preceding fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' meeting recorded in the statutory Minute Book; no government filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be held within six months after each fiscal year-end (by 30 June for a calendar-year SL)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene or approve the annual accounts prevents their deposit; continued neglect leads to Commercial Registry closure and administrative fines under the Ley de Sociedades de Capital.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of Annual Accounts (Depósito de Cuentas Anuales) – balance sheet, profit and loss, statement of changes in equity, and explanatory notes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil de la provincia (Provincial Commercial Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: File within one month after approval and within seven months of the balance-sheet date; for a calendar-year SL, approval by 30 June and deposit by 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Commercial Registry closure (cierre registral) preventing registration of all subsequent deeds, share transfers, and appointments; ICAC fines of EUR 3,000 to EUR 12,000 per fiscal year; persistent non-filing may trigger administrative dissolution or strike-off of the SL.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual legalization of statutory books (Legalización de Libros del Registro Mercantil)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil de la provincia (Provincial Commercial Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Before use of new annual books or within four months after the close of each fiscal year (by 30 April for a calendar-year SL)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unlegalized books lose evidentiary value in commercial and legal proceedings; the Commercial Registry may impose a fine and withhold subsequent registrations until presentation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO register confirmation and update (Libro Registro de Titulares Reales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal statutory register; public deed and Provincial Commercial Registry filing only when share transfers affect substantial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Reviewed and confirmed at the ordinary annual general meeting; any change in beneficial ownership above 25% or control must be reflected before the next deposit of annual accounts, with the deed filed within ten business days of the transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: AML Law 10/2010 penalties for inaccurate or missing UBO registers, ranging from EUR 600 to EUR 10,000; breaches in serious cases up to EUR 1,000,000; failure to update the Members' Register triggers registry closure for share-transfer deeds.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada must undergo a statutory audit when, for two consecutive years, it satisfies at least two of the following three criteria: (a) annual net turnover exceeds EUR 5,700,000; (b) total assets exceed EUR 2,850,000; (c) average number of employees exceeds 50. A software company using remote-support IOT telemetry and collecting revenue only through Stripe/Paddle normally falls below these thresholds, so no mandatory audit is required.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish GAAP (Plan General de Contabilidad, R.D. 1514/2007) for individual accounts; PGC-PyME permitted for entities below the audit-exemption thresholds; IFRS-EU required only for consolidated groups, which is not applicable to a single Spanish SL.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No external annual UBO return is required. The SL must maintain and continuously update its Libro Registro de Titulares Reales. At each ordinary general meeting the administrator certifies that the ledger reflects all current beneficial owners. Any share transfer creating or altering a 25% or controlling stake must be formalized by public deed, recorded in the Members' Register, and deposited at the Commercial Registry before the annual accounts deposit deadline. Given the low-risk software business using standard payment rails, simplified due diligence applies for UBO identification.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Directors (Libro Registro de Consejeros / Actas del Consejo, as applicable)
Minute Book (Libro de Actas de la Junta General)
Beneficial Owners Ledger (Libro Registro de Titulares Reales)
Accounting Diary and Inventory (Libro Diario y Libro de Inventarios y Cuentas Anuales)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $600 - $2,200 (annual outsourcing of registered office, asesoría, and corporate maintenance services)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% general rate of the Spanish corporate income tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades, IS) under Art 29.1 Ley 27/2014 (LIS). A newly formed SL may enjoy a reduced 15% headline rate for the first two taxable years in which a positive taxable base arises, provided the conditions in Art 29.2 LIS are met (minimum paid-in share capital, no prior dissolved entity continuation, no negative equity, and the reduction is applied to the profit before the corporate income tax credit).
